topicName: GitHub Actions: Workflows, Runners, Actions, and Secrets Management
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering GitHub Actions: Workflows, Runners, Actions, and Secrets Management"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines are essential for modern software development. GitHub Actions provides a powerful, native automation platform directly within your repositories. This tutorial covers the core components of GitHub Actions and how to manage them securely."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding GitHub Workflows"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A workflow is a configurable automated process that will run one or more jobs. Workflows are defined by YAML files stored in the .github/workflows directory of your repository. An event in your repository, such as a push or a pull request, can trigger a workflow."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"name: CI Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Exploring Runners"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"A runner is a server that runs your workflows when they are triggered. You can use GitHub-hosted runners or host your own self-hosted runners for specialized hardware and security requirements."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"GitHub-hosted runners: Managed and maintained by GitHub, running on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Self-hosted runners: Configured and managed by you to run in your own data center or cloud environment."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Utilizing Actions"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Actions are individual tasks that you can combine as steps to create a job. You can write your own actions, or use community-created actions from the GitHub Marketplace using the 'uses' keyword."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"- name: Set up Node.js
  uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Secrets Management"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Never hardcode sensitive data like API keys, passwords, or deployment credentials in your workflow files. Instead, use GitHub Secrets. Secrets are encrypted environment variables stored securely in your repository or organization settings."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"- name: Deploy to Production
  env:
    API_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_API_KEY }}
  run: ./deploy.sh"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To add secrets, navigate to your repository settings, click on 'Secrets and variables', select 'Actions', and click 'New repository secret'. You can then reference them in your workflow using the '${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}' syntax."}]
